evidence.statement: The 17-bp exact sequence GCAAGACGGAAAGACCC appears in five qualifying E. coli↔yeast-mitochondrial same-diagonal clusters in the frozen all-pair scan; the yeast coordinate is the same chrM start0 59,956 in each cluster, paired to five distinct E. coli starts.
The frozen yeast chrM start0 59,956 corresponds to 1-based 59,957, which lies inside the independently recorded post-freeze S. cerevisiae mitochondrial 21S_RRNA/Q0158 locus 58,009–62,447.

The yeast-side occurrence is therefore part of the same large-subunit-rRNA neighborhood already validated in Proof Case 0001; the E. coli semantic identity of the five matching occurrences is deliberately left UNKNOWN pending assembly-matched annotation validation.
Post-freeze assembly-matched validation confirms all five E. coli occurrences fall inside annotated 23S rRNA genes rrlH, rrlC, rrlA, rrlB, and rrlE.
LC-PRIM-0006 is therefore a validated exact large-subunit-rRNA-associated primitive shared between multiple bacterial 23S rRNA copies and yeast mitochondrial 21S rRNA.
LC-PRIM-0006 contains the published E. coli 23S sequence ACGGAAAGACCC corresponding to positions 2054-2065, fixing the full primitive at positions 2049-2065.

The primitive overlaps the Domain V catalytic/antibiotic-recognition neighborhood, includes A2058 and G2061, and substantially overlaps the sequence-specific TLR13 recognition element reported at 2054-2068.

Coder alias: LSU_PTC_GATE — a deeply conserved token positioned at the transition into the peptidyl-transferase catalytic neighborhood and also used as an antibiotic/innate-immune recognition surface.

unknowns: Assembly-matched annotation of the five E. coli occurrences.
Mechanistic role of the exact 17-bp sequence.
